t: This is Christ Church Spitalfields, on Commercial Street, facing the City of London across the border. It was built between 1714 and 1729 to a design by Nicholas Hawksmoor. It was one of the first of the Commissioners' Churches, built for the Commission for Building Fifty New Churches, which an act of parliament established in 1711. Hawksmoor was a leading figure of English Baroque, and worked alongside Christopher Wren and John Vanbrugh, contributing to St Paul's Cathedral, Greenwich Hospital and Blenheim Palace.
